# 2.1 RNA Bulk Dataset

Dataset: **GSE164416** (Wigger et al. 2021, *Nature Metabolism*), pancreatic
islet RNA-seq. 133 raw samples; this project uses the ND/IGT/T2D subset
(98 samples after QC), excluding T3cD samples as pancreatogenic diabetes falls
outside the ND -> IGT -> T2D progression pathway this project is modelling.

Corresponds to: `scripts/00_download_data.R`, `scripts/01_prepare_metadata.R`
(the two were later split; the current repo keeps the metadata-building logic
in `01_prepare_metadata.R` and the raw pull in `00_download_data.R`).

```{r download-and-annotate, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/00_download_data.R
# GSE164416 supplementary file URL
count_url <- paste0(
  "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE164nnn/",
  "GSE164416/suppl/GSE164416_DP_htseq_counts.txt.gz"
)

if (!file.exists(count_gz)) {
  download.file(count_url, count_gz, mode = "wb")
}
R.utils::gunzip(count_gz, remove = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

# GEO Series Matrix file containing sample annotations
gse_list  <- GEOquery::getGEO("GSE164416", GSEMatrix = TRUE, destdir = raw_dir)
gse_object <- gse_list[[1]]
geo_pheno  <- Biobase::pData(gse_object)

counts_df <- data.table::fread(count_txt)
count_matrix <- counts_df %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames(var = colnames(counts_df)[1]) %>%
  as.matrix()
mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"
```

Clinical metadata (age, BMI, HbA1c, 2h glycaemia) was not in the GEO record
itself - it's only in the paper's Supplementary Table 1, which needed a Nature
subscription to access before I found the direct supplementary-file link. That
file (`42255_2021_420_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx`) is merged with the GEO phenotype table
by donor ID:

```{r merge-clinical-metadata, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/00_download_data.R
clinical_data <- readxl::read_excel(clinical_xlsx, sheet = 1, col_names = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    donor_id = 1, diabetes_status_clinical = 2, age_clinical = 3,
    glycaemia_2h_ogtt = 4, hba1c_clinical = 5, bmi_clinical = 6
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    donor_id = stringr::str_trim(donor_id),
    # Note: supplementary file uses "T3D" instead of "T3cD"
    status_clinical = dplyr::case_when(
      diabetes_status_clinical == "ND"  ~ "ND",
      diabetes_status_clinical == "IGT" ~ "IGT",
      diabetes_status_clinical == "T2D" ~ "T2D",
      diabetes_status_clinical %in% c("T3D", "T3cD") ~ "T3cD",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    age = as.numeric(age_clinical),
    bmi = as.numeric(bmi_clinical),
    hba1c = as.numeric(hba1c_clinical),
    glycaemia_2h = as.numeric(glycaemia_2h_ogtt)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(donor_id, status_clinical, age, bmi, hba1c, glycaemia_2h)

sample_metadata <- tibble(
  sample   = sample_names,
  donor_id = stringr::str_extract(sample_names, "DP\\d+")
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(geo_metadata, by = "donor_id") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(clinical_data, by = "donor_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::coalesce(status_clinical, status_geo))
```

Genes are annotated with symbol/name (`org.Hs.eg.db`, used offline because the
Ensembl biomart kept timing out) and biotype (parsed directly from the
GENCODE v46 GTF, since `org.Hs.eg.db` doesn't carry biotype):

```{r gene-annotation, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/00_download_data.R
gene_ids_clean <- stringr::str_remove(gene_ids, "\\.[0-9]+$")

gene_annotation <- tibble(
  original_gene_id = gene_ids,
  ensembl_gene_id   = gene_ids_clean
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene_symbol = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
      org.Hs.eg.db, keys = ensembl_gene_id,
      column = "SYMBOL", keytype = "ENSEMBL", multiVals = "first"
    ) %>% unname()
  )

# GTF attributes format: gene_id "ENSG...5"; gene_type "..."; gene_name "...";
gtf_gene_df <- tibble(line = gene_lines) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ensembl_gene_id_versioned = stringr::str_match(line, 'gene_id "([^"]+)"')[, 2],
    gene_name_gtf = stringr::str_match(line, 'gene_name "([^"]+)"')[, 2],
    biotype       = stringr::str_match(line, 'gene_type "([^"]+)"')[, 2]
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ensembl_gene_id = stringr::str_remove(ensembl_gene_id_versioned, "\\.[0-9]+$")) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()
```

# 2.2 GSE164416 Pre-Processing

`scripts/00A_fastq_to_counts.sh` documents the raw FASTQ -> counts pipeline
(SRA download, FastQC/MultiQC, fastp trimming, STAR 2-pass alignment,
HTSeq-count) that *would* reproduce the author-supplied count matrix from
scratch. It was authored and dry-run checked (`DRY_RUN=TRUE`) rather than
executed against the real 133 samples, since the sequencing toolchain
(sra-tools/STAR/HTSeq) wasn't installed locally and a full run needs ~500GB of
disk. All downstream analysis uses the GEO-deposited count matrix directly.

```{bash fastq-pipeline-config, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/00A_fastq_to_counts.sh
# --- User-configurable settings ---
THREADS=8
DRY_RUN=TRUE        # set to true to print commands without running

# DATASET:
#   GEO: GSE164416   |  SRA: SRP300812  |  BioProject: PRJNA690574
#   Reference genome: GRCh38 (hg38)  |  Annotation: GENCODE v46

# Full list of 133 SRA run accessions for GSE164416
SRA_ACCESSIONS=(
    SRR13193797 SRR13193798 SRR13193799 SRR13193800 SRR13193801
    SRR13193802 SRR13193803 SRR13193804 SRR13193805 SRR13193806
    # ... (133 accessions total, see scripts/00A_fastq_to_counts.sh)
)

# PIPELINE STEPS:
#   1. Download raw FASTQ (prefetch / fasterq-dump)
#   2. FastQC + MultiQC on raw reads
#   3. Adapter trimming (fastp)
#   4. FastQC + MultiQC on trimmed reads
#   5. Build STAR genome index (GRCh38 + GENCODE v46 GTF)
#   6. STAR 2-pass alignment
#   7. Sort/index BAM (SAMtools)
#   8. Alignment QC (RSeQC / samtools flagstat)
#   9. Gene-level counting (HTSeq-count)
#  10. Merge per-sample counts into one count matrix
```

# 2.3 Gene Filtering and Normalisation

Corresponds to: `scripts/02_qc_filter_normalise.R`. Subsets to the 98
ND/IGT/T2D samples, removes low-count genes, and VST-transforms
(`blind = TRUE`, i.e. without using disease-status labels).

```{r qc-subset-and-filter, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/02_qc_filter_normalise.R
sample_metadata_subset <- sample_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(status %in% c("ND", "IGT", "T2D")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(status = factor(status, levels = c("ND", "IGT", "T2D")))

count_matrix_subset <- count_matrix[, sample_metadata_subset$sample, drop = FALSE]

stopifnot(identical(colnames(count_matrix_subset), sample_metadata_subset$sample))

# Filter lowly expressed genes: count >= 10 in at least 20% of samples
min_count   <- 10
min_samples <- ceiling(0.20 * ncol(count_matrix_subset))
keep_genes  <- rowSums(count_matrix_subset >= min_count) >= min_samples

count_matrix_filtered <- count_matrix_subset[keep_genes, , drop = FALSE]
# 58,336 genes -> ~20,042 genes retained after this filter
```

```{r qc-deseq-vst, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/02_qc_filter_normalise.R
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(count_matrix_filtered),
  colData   = as.data.frame(sample_metadata_subset),
  design    = ~ status
)
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)
normalized_counts <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)

# VST chosen over rlog for this sample size; blind = TRUE so the transform
# does not use the disease-status labels (avoids leaking group info into
# a step that's meant to be an unsupervised variance stabilisation)
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)

saveRDS(dds, file.path(qc_data_dir, "dds_qc_ready.rds"))
saveRDS(vsd, file.path(qc_data_dir, "vsd_qc_ready.rds"))
```

PCA and sample-distance heatmaps were used to check for outliers before
freezing this matrix for downstream use:

```{r qc-pca, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/02_qc_filter_normalise.R
vsd_matrix  <- assay(vsd)
pca_result  <- prcomp(t(vsd_matrix), scale. = TRUE)
percent_var <- round(100 * (pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2)), 1)

pca_scatter <- ggplot(pca_coords, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = status)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.85) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Variance-Stabilized Counts",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", percent_var[1], "% variance)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", percent_var[2], "% variance)")
  )
```

# 2.4 Differential Expression Analysis

Corresponds to: `scripts/03_differential_expression.R`. DESeq2, Wald test,
three pairwise contrasts (ND as reference level), BH-adjusted, threshold
`padj < 0.05 & |log2FC| > 1`.

```{r de-build-dds, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/03_differential_expression.R
sample_metadata <- sample_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(sample %in% colnames(count_matrix_filtered)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(status = factor(status, levels = c("ND", "IGT", "T2D")))
sample_metadata <- sample_metadata[match(colnames(count_matrix_filtered), sample_metadata$sample), ]

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(count_matrix_filtered),
  colData   = as.data.frame(sample_metadata),
  design    = ~status
)
dds$status <- relevel(dds$status, ref = "ND")

dds <- DESeq(dds)   # negative binomial GLM + empirical Bayes dispersion shrinkage
```

```{r de-contrasts, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/03_differential_expression.R
annotate_results <- function(res_object, gene_annotation_table) {
  as.data.frame(res_object) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "gene_id") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      gene_annotation_table %>% dplyr::select(original_gene_id, gene_symbol, gene_name, biotype),
      by = c("gene_id" = "original_gene_id")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(padj, dplyr::desc(abs(log2FoldChange)))
}

extract_significant <- function(res_df, padj_cutoff = 0.05, lfc_cutoff = 1) {
  res_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(padj < padj_cutoff, abs(log2FoldChange) > lfc_cutoff)
}

run_comparison <- function(dds_object, numerator, denominator, gene_annotation_table) {
  res <- results(dds_object, contrast = c("status", numerator, denominator), alpha = 0.05)
  res_df <- annotate_results(res, gene_annotation_table)
  list(res = res, full = res_df, sig = extract_significant(res_df),
       lncrna = extract_significant(res_df) %>% dplyr::filter(biotype == "lncRNA"))
}

comparison_igt_vs_nd  <- run_comparison(dds, "IGT", "ND",  gene_annotation)
comparison_t2d_vs_nd  <- run_comparison(dds, "T2D", "ND",  gene_annotation)
comparison_t2d_vs_igt <- run_comparison(dds, "T2D", "IGT", gene_annotation)
```

## 2.4.1 Covariate-Adjusted Sensitivity Analysis

Corresponds to: `scripts/C1_de_covariate_adjusted.R`. Age (ANOVA p = 0.0077)
and BMI (p = 0.0146) differed significantly across ND/IGT/T2D, so the primary
status-only model was re-fit with both as covariates, as a parallel sensitivity
check rather than a replacement model.

```{r covariate-anova-check, eval=FALSE}
# ANOVA check that motivated C1 (run interactively before writing C1)
summary(aov(age ~ status, data = sample_metadata))   # p = 0.0077
summary(aov(bmi ~ status, data = sample_metadata))   # p = 0.0146
```

```{r covariate-adjusted-model, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/C1_de_covariate_adjusted.R
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(count_matrix_filtered),
  colData   = as.data.frame(sample_metadata),
  design    = ~age + bmi + status
)
dds$status <- relevel(dds$status, ref = "ND")
dds <- DESeq(dds)

comparisons <- list(
  T2D_vs_ND  = c("T2D", "ND"),
  IGT_vs_ND  = c("IGT", "ND"),
  T2D_vs_IGT = c("T2D", "IGT")
)

for (name in names(comparisons)) {
  res    <- results(dds, contrast = c("status", comparisons[[name]][1], comparisons[[name]][2]), alpha = 0.05)
  res_df <- annotate_results(res, gene_annotation)
  sig_df <- extract_significant(res_df)
  readr::write_tsv(sig_df, file.path(out_tables_dir, paste0("DESeq2_", name, "_covariate_adjusted_significant.tsv")))
}
```

```{r covariate-overlap, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/C1_de_covariate_adjusted.R - comparing adjusted vs primary DEG lists
orig_genes <- unique(orig_sig$gene_id)
new_genes  <- unique(new_sig$gene_id)

n_shared <- length(intersect(orig_genes, new_genes))
n_lost   <- length(setdiff(orig_genes, new_genes))
n_gained <- length(setdiff(new_genes, orig_genes))
pct_survived <- round(100 * n_shared / length(orig_genes), 1)
# T2D vs ND: 452/604 shared -> 74.8% of primary DEGs survive covariate adjustment
```

# 2.5 Long Non-Coding RNA Prioritisation

Corresponds to: `scripts/04_lncrna_prioritisation.R`. Each significant lncRNA
per comparison gets a composite score (mean of three min-max rescaled 0-1
components), plus a separate recurrence score aggregated across all three
comparisons.

```{r lncrna-rescale-helper, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/04_lncrna_prioritisation.R
rescale_01 <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(rep(NA_real_, length(x)))
  rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (diff(rng) == 0) return(rep(1, length(x)))
  (x - rng[1]) / (rng[2] - rng[1])
}
```

```{r lncrna-prioritisation-score, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/04_lncrna_prioritisation.R
prioritise_lncrna <- function(lnc_df, comparison_label) {
  lnc_df %>%
    left_join(mean_expression, by = "gene_id") %>%
    mutate(
      abs_log2FC      = abs(log2FoldChange),
      neg_log10_padj  = if_else(!is.na(padj) & padj > 0, -log10(padj), NA_real_)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      score_padj = rescale_01(neg_log10_padj),
      score_lfc  = rescale_01(abs_log2FC),
      score_expr = rescale_01(log1p(mean_normalized_expression))
    ) %>%
    mutate(prioritisation_score = (score_padj + score_lfc + score_expr) / 3) %>%
    arrange(desc(prioritisation_score)) %>%
    mutate(prioritisation_rank = row_number(), comparison = comparison_label)
}

ranked_igt_vs_nd  <- prioritise_lncrna(lnc_igt_vs_nd,  "IGT vs ND")
ranked_t2d_vs_nd  <- prioritise_lncrna(lnc_t2d_vs_nd,  "T2D vs ND")
ranked_t2d_vs_igt <- prioritise_lncrna(lnc_t2d_vs_igt, "T2D vs IGT")
```

```{r lncrna-recurrence, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/04_lncrna_prioritisation.R
cross_comparison_summary <- all_ranked_long %>%
  group_by(gene_id, gene_symbol, gene_name, biotype) %>%
  summarise(
    comparisons_present     = n(),
    max_prioritisation_score = max(prioritisation_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    recurrence_score     = comparisons_present / 3,
    global_priority_score = (recurrence_score + max_prioritisation_score) / 2
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(global_priority_score))
```

# 2.6 WGCNA Network Construction

Corresponds to: `scripts/05A_prepare_wgcna_inputs.R` (input QC,
`goodSamplesGenes()`) and `scripts/05B_wgcna_construct_network.R` (soft
threshold selection, `blockwiseModules()`, module-trait correlation).

```{r wgcna-input-qc, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/05A_prepare_wgcna_inputs.R
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
disableWGCNAThreads()

datExpr0 <- as.data.frame(t(expr_mat))   # transpose: samples as rows, genes as columns

gsg <- WGCNA::goodSamplesGenes(datExpr1, verbose = 3)
if (!gsg$allOK) {
  datExpr1 <- datExpr1[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes, drop = FALSE]
}
```

```{r wgcna-soft-threshold, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/05B_wgcna_construct_network.R
powers <- c(1:10, seq(12, 30, by = 2))

sft <- pickSoftThreshold(
  datExpr,
  powerVector = powers,
  networkType = "signed",
  corFnc      = "bicor",                       # bi-weight midcorrelation, robust to outliers
  corOptions  = list(maxPOutliers = 0.1),
  verbose = 5
)

fit_df <- tibble(
  Power = sft$fitIndices[, 1],
  SFT_R2 = -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2]
)

# Lowest power exceeding R^2 >= 0.80
candidate_powers <- fit_df %>% filter(SFT_R2 >= 0.80)
soft_power <- if (nrow(candidate_powers) > 0) min(candidate_powers$Power) else fit_df$Power[which.max(fit_df$SFT_R2)]
# soft_power = 8 (R^2 = 0.85)
```

```{r wgcna-blockwise-modules, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/05B_wgcna_construct_network.R
net <- blockwiseModules(
  datExpr,
  power       = soft_power,
  corType     = "bicor",
  maxPOutliers = 0.1,
  networkType = "signed",
  TOMType     = "signed",
  minModuleSize   = 30,
  reassignThreshold = 0,
  mergeCutHeight  = 0.25,
  numericLabels   = FALSE,
  pamRespectsDendro = TRUE,
  saveTOMs = FALSE,      # full 20,042-gene TOM not saved: memory/runtime cost
  deepSplit = 2,
  verbose = 5
)

module_colors     <- net$colors
module_eigengenes <- orderMEs(net$MEs)
# 30 modules detected (including grey) across 20,042 genes
```

```{r wgcna-module-trait-correlation, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/05B_wgcna_construct_network.R
safe_cor_p <- function(x, y) {
  out <- tryCatch(cor.test(x, y, method = "pearson"), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(out)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  c(unname(out$estimate), out$p.value)
}

# 240 module x trait tests (raw p-values; BH-corrected post hoc since
# cor.test() itself does not adjust for multiple comparisons)
for (i in seq_along(module_names)) {
  for (j in seq_along(trait_names)) {
    x <- ME_mat[[module_names[i]]]
    y <- trait_data_numeric[[trait_names[j]]]
    keep <- complete.cases(x, y)
    if (sum(keep) >= 10) {
      tmp <- safe_cor_p(x[keep], y[keep])
      cor_mat[i, j] <- tmp[1]
      p_mat[i, j]   <- tmp[2]
    }
  }
}
```

Hub-gene visualisation used a TOM recomputed only for the top 20 hub genes per
focus module (160 genes total), exported via `WGCNA::exportNetworkToCytoscape()`
(see `scripts/W1_tom_heatmap.R`), rather than exporting the full 20,042-gene TOM.

# 2.7 Module-Trait Correlation and Hub Gene Scoring

Corresponds to: `scripts/05C_hub_gene_prioritisation.R`. Focus modules are the
union of (a) trait-associated modules, (b) a default set of interpretable
mid-sized modules, and (c) any module containing a top-20 prioritised lncRNA
not already captured.

```{r hub-focus-modules, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/05C_hub_gene_prioritisation.R
default_focus_modules <- c("brown", "yellow", "green", "red", "black")

module_interest <- module_trait_summary %>%
  filter(trait %in% c("status_ND", "status_IGT", "status_T2D")) %>%
  mutate(module_clean = gsub("^ME", "", module)) %>%
  filter(module_clean != "grey") %>%
  arrange(p_value, desc(abs(correlation)))

overlap_modules <- intersect(default_focus_modules, module_interest$module_clean)
focus_modules <- if (length(overlap_modules) >= 3) overlap_modules else default_focus_modules

# then: add any module containing a top-20 prioritised lncRNA not already in focus_modules
# (see full logic in scripts/05C_hub_gene_prioritisation.R)
# -> 8 focus modules, 5,760 genes total
```

```{r hub-score-composite, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/05C_hub_gene_prioritisation.R
minmax_rescale <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(rng[1], rng[2]))) return(rep(1, length(x)))
  (x - rng[1]) / (rng[2] - rng[1])
}

# Module membership (kME) = correlation of each gene with its module eigengene
kME_mat <- as.data.frame(cor(datExpr, ME_mat, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson"))

# Gene significance (GS) = correlation of each gene with disease status / clinical traits
gs_cor <- apply(datExpr, 2, function(g) safe_cor(g, traits_df[["status_T2D"]]))

hub_tbl_focus <- hub_tbl_focus %>%
  mutate(
    score_kME  = minmax_rescale(abs_own_kME),
    score_GS   = minmax_rescale(priority_gs),      # GSabs_status_T2D preferred when available
    score_DE   = minmax_rescale(de_strength),       # -log10(padj) from T2D vs ND
    score_LFC  = minmax_rescale(de_lfc_abs)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hub_score_all_genes = rowMeans(cbind(score_kME, score_GS, score_DE, score_LFC), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

hub_ranked_all <- hub_tbl_focus %>%
  group_by(module_color) %>%
  arrange(desc(hub_score_all_genes), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(hub_rank_all_genes = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()
```

# 2.8 lncRNA Network Integration

Corresponds to: `scripts/06_lncrna_annotation.R`. Weighted integration score
(unlike the unweighted composites in 2.5/2.7), designed so lncRNA-specific
evidence (priority + recurrence, 50%) outweighs generic network-position
evidence (module correlation + hub centrality + gene significance, 50%).

```{r lncrna-network-integration-score, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/06_lncrna_annotation.R
rescale01 <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (diff(rng) == 0) return(ifelse(is.na(x), NA_real_, 1))
  (x - rng[1]) / (rng[2] - rng[1])
}

lnc_module_tbl <- lnc_module_tbl %>%
  mutate(
    score_lnc_priority = rescale01(prioritisationscore),
    score_recurrence   = rescale01(recurrencescore),
    score_module_cor   = rescale01(abs(best_cor)),
    score_hub_central  = rescale01(abs_own_kME),
    score_gs           = rescale01(priority_gs)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    network_integration_score =
      0.30 * score_lnc_priority +
      0.20 * score_recurrence   +
      0.20 * score_module_cor   +
      0.15 * score_hub_central  +
      0.15 * score_gs
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(network_integration_score))

# Complete-case criterion: only lncRNAs with a valid module assignment AND
# non-missing values across all five components get a non-missing score
lnc_candidates_network <- lnc_module_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(module_color), !is.na(network_integration_score))
```

# 2.9 Functional Enrichment Analysis

Corresponds to: `scripts/07_enrichment_analysis.R`. `clusterProfiler`
`enrichGO`/`enrichKEGG`, Ensembl -> Entrez via `org.Hs.eg.db`, BH-adjusted
(q < 0.05), one enrichment set per DE comparison and per WGCNA focus module.

```{r enrichment-id-mapping, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/07_enrichment_analysis.R
strip_version <- function(x) sub("\\.\\d+$", "", x)

ensembl_to_entrez <- function(ensembl_ids) {
  mapping <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    org.Hs.eg.db,
    keys = strip_version(ensembl_ids),
    columns = c("ENSEMBL", "ENTREZID", "SYMBOL"),
    keytype = "ENSEMBL"
  )
  mapping[!is.na(mapping$ENTREZID) & !duplicated(mapping$ENSEMBL), ]
}

# Universe = union of all tested genes across the three DE comparisons
universe_ensembl <- unique(unlist(lapply(de_all, function(d) d$gene_id)))
universe_map    <- ensembl_to_entrez(strip_version(na.omit(universe_ensembl)))
universe_entrez <- unique(na.omit(universe_map$ENTREZID))
# 20,042 tested genes -> 17,000 (83.8%) mapped to Entrez
```

```{r enrichment-go-kegg, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/07_enrichment_analysis.R
run_go_enrich <- function(gene_entrez, universe_entrez, label, ont = "BP") {
  if (length(gene_entrez) < 5) return(NULL)
  enrichGO(
    gene = gene_entrez, universe = universe_entrez, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
    ont = ont, pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.2,
    readable = TRUE
  )
}

run_kegg_enrich <- function(gene_entrez, universe_entrez, label) {
  if (length(gene_entrez) < 5) return(NULL)
  enrichKEGG(
    gene = gene_entrez, universe = universe_entrez, organism = "hsa",
    pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.2
  )
}

for (cmp in names(de_sig)) {
  sig_entrez <- unique(na.omit(ensembl_to_entrez(strip_version(de_sig[[cmp]]$gene_id))$ENTREZID))
  go_bp <- run_go_enrich(sig_entrez, universe_entrez, cmp, ont = "BP")
  go_mf <- run_go_enrich(sig_entrez, universe_entrez, cmp, ont = "MF")
  kegg  <- run_kegg_enrich(sig_entrez, universe_entrez, cmp)
}

for (mod in focus_modules) {
  mod_entrez <- unique(na.omit(ensembl_to_entrez(strip_version(
    module_assignments$gene_id[module_assignments$module_color == mod]
  ))$ENTREZID))
  go_bp <- run_go_enrich(mod_entrez, universe_entrez, mod, ont = "BP")
}
```

# 2.10 Machine Learning Classification

Two layers of ML code exist in this repo:

* `scripts/08_ml_models.py` - the main classification pipeline (RF, L2
  logistic regression, RBF-SVM, XGBoost+SHAP) using standard 5-fold
  stratified CV on hub genes selected from the full 98-sample WGCNA run.
* `scripts/N0-N5_*` - a leakage check written after noticing that the hub
  genes fed into script 08 were selected using module-trait correlation
  computed across *all* 98 samples, including each CV fold's own held-out
  labels. The `N` scripts redo feature selection (WGCNA + hub scoring)
  train-only, then evaluate once on a held-out split that never influenced
  feature selection - this is the "nested cross-validation" framing described
  in the methodology text (outer estimate of generalisation performance;
  inner loop restricted to the training fold only).

```{r ml-cv-setup, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/08_ml_models.py (shown here for reference - runs as Python)
```

```{python ml-classifiers, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/08_ml_models.py
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)

models = {
    "RandomForest": Pipeline([
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("clf", RandomForestClassifier(
            n_estimators=300, max_features="sqrt", class_weight="balanced",
            random_state=42, n_jobs=-1))
    ]),
    "LogisticRegression": Pipeline([
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("clf", LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=2000, class_weight="balanced",
                                    solver="lbfgs", random_state=42))
    ]),
    "SVM_RBF": Pipeline([
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("clf", SVC(kernel="rbf", C=1.0, probability=True,
                     class_weight="balanced", random_state=42))
    ]),
}

for name, model in models.items():
    cv_result = cross_validate(model, X_bin, y_bin, cv=cv,
                                scoring=["roc_auc", "balanced_accuracy"])
    y_prob = cross_val_predict(model, X_bin, y_bin, cv=cv, method="predict_proba")[:, 1]
```

```{python ml-permutation-test, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/08_ml_models.py
N_PERMUTATIONS = 100  # halves runtime vs 200 for equivalent p-value resolution (1/N)

score, perm_scores, pvalue = permutation_test_score(
    models[best_model_name], X_bin, y_bin,
    scoring="roc_auc", cv=cv, n_permutations=N_PERMUTATIONS,
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)
```

```{python ml-rf-gini-importance, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/08_ml_models.py - Gini (mean decrease in impurity) importance
rf_model.fit(X_bin, y_bin)
rf_clf = rf_model.named_steps["clf"]

importances = pd.Series(
    rf_clf.feature_importances_, index=feature_names
).sort_values(ascending=False)

# Permutation importance as a more reliable companion estimate
perm_imp = permutation_importance(
    rf_model, X_bin, y_bin, n_repeats=50, random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1, scoring="roc_auc"
)
```

```{python ml-shap-xgboost, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/08_ml_models.py
xgb_model = xgb.XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=300, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05,
    subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8,
    objective="binary:logistic", eval_metric="logloss",
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1
)

xgb_model.fit(X_scaled_bin, y_bin)
explainer   = shap.TreeExplainer(xgb_model)
shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X_scaled_bin)

mean_shap = pd.DataFrame({
    "gene": feature_names,
    "mean_shap": np.abs(shap_values).mean(axis=0),
}).sort_values("mean_shap", ascending=False)
```

```{r nested-cv-train-test-split, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/N1_nested_split.R - the leakage-free split used by N2-N5
set.seed(SEED)

# Stratified 80/20 split by status, done BEFORE any WGCNA/hub-gene step
# touches the held-out samples
split_list <- lapply(split(traits$sampleid, traits$status), function(ids) {
  n_test   <- max(1, round(length(ids) * 0.2))
  test_ids <- sample(ids, n_test)
  data.frame(sampleid = ids, split = ifelse(ids %in% test_ids, "test", "train"))
})
split_df <- bind_rows(split_list)
```

```{python nested-cv-holdout-eval, eval=FALSE}
# from scripts/N4_nested_ml_validation.py
# Feature set: hub genes selected using ONLY the 78 TRAIN samples
# (from N0 train-only DE, N2 train-only WGCNA, N3 train-only hub scoring -
# none of which ever saw the 20 held-out samples' labels)
hub_genes = (
    hub_df.sort_values("hub_rank_all_genes")
    .groupby("module_color").head(10)["gene_id"].unique().tolist()
)

X_train = X_full.loc[train_bin].values
y_train = (traits_df.loc[train_bin, "status"] == "T2D").astype(int).values
X_test  = X_full.loc[test_bin].values
y_test  = (traits_df.loc[test_bin, "status"] == "T2D").astype(int).values

# fit on TRAIN, evaluate ONCE on the never-touched held-out TEST samples
for name, model in models.items():
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
```
